testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Go straight forward, then straight back.
Go straight back, then forward to the left.
Go straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, go straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must keep ____ points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact as you exit. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts may show that they are loose.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to prevent:

options.text: Ice from forming in the brake system.
People from breathing the air in the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: When driving, it is important that you:

options.text: Plan what to do if dangerous situations happen.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan what to do if dangerous situations happen.
questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Plan what you will do if hazards turn into emergencies.

questions.question: To prevent drowsiness while driving, you should:

options.text: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before your trip. Have someone ride with you. Take trips when you are normally awake. Avoid medicines that make you drowsy. Regular exercise can help you stay alert.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Rely only on what other drivers do to tell you if a train is coming.
Not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not depend only on warning signals, gates, or flaggers to alert you to trains. Be extra alert at crossings without gates or signals. At any crossing, assume a train is coming.

questions.question: In cold temperatures, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Use extra caution on bridges and overpasses when driving in cold, wet conditions.

questions.question: If you see a construction worker near the road in a construction zone where you are already driving slowly, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down more.
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly through construction zones. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When you pull off to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is a problem with transporting hanging meat in a trailer?

options.text: It is not recommended during summer months.
Animals may be attracted to the smell of the meat.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can make the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights to show when the system is not working.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. These lights alert you when the braking system is not working. Find out where this light is located in your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: When you come to a railroad crossing during a driving test, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During a driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What part between the air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way check valve
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: If you notice a safety issue or possible mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Wait to see if the problem fixes itself.
Write about it in your vehicle report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write about it in your vehicle report.
questions.explanation: After driving, you may need to write a report about your vehicle's condition. Always mention anything that could affect safety or cause mechanical problems.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include explosives such as ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, you need to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level correctly.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight capacity of your suspension system.
Put light items under heavy items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight capacity of your suspension system.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your vehicle is not overloaded. You must know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension system rating.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to operate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use air brakes. An air brake system uses compressed air to work.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Remove wheel chocks and release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brakes. The warning signal should turn on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They help drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved, convex mirrors. They allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What happens when cargo is loaded with a high center of gravity?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to roll over.
Items are more likely to fall down.
It becomes harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Cargo should be loaded with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob outward to apply the parking brakes. Push it inward to release them.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: People exit quickly and may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People exit quickly and may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may be in a hurry and pull into traffic without warning. They may also step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and road
The time it takes to apply the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. Good traction is needed for safe braking and steering.

questions.question: What happens after two violations for hand-held phone use while driving?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
You must drive 10 mph slower than the speed limit for a set time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your CDL will be disqualified.
questions.explanation: Two convictions for hand-held phone use will disqualify your CDL. Penalties increase with more violations.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include: trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, wandering thoughts, trouble remembering miles driven, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping head up, drifting from lane, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coming out of tunnels.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep a vehicle in its lane. Wind is especially dangerous when exiting a tunnel.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. This is especially true when carrying a heavy load.

questions.question: When driving under bridges and overpasses, you should:

options.text: Not trust the posted clearance height.
Measure the opening before driving through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not trust the posted clearance height.
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height clearances. The road may have been repaved, or snow may be on the ground. The actual height may be different from the sign. If you are unsure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads. Cut your speed by about one-third when driving on wet surfaces.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test for a CDL, you may be asked to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A low air pressure warning device.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A low air pressure warning device.
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three minutes.
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the instrument panel.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look occurs when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. You can use one look during straight line backing. You can use up to two looks during other exercises.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, a person must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Able to perform their own background check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose this endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how short.

questions.question: When looking into the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking the fifth wheel coupling, look into the gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes wear out faster than properly adjusted ones. Check your brakes often to avoid problems.

questions.question: If you must drive on the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as you can.
Get both sets of wheels completely on the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop completely. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Avoid hard braking on the shoulder above 20 mph. Keep one set of wheels on the road if you can.

questions.question: How should you perform pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Change your routine each time to focus on different items.
Follow the same routine each time to avoid missing anything.
Do them once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same routine each time to avoid missing anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This habit helps you remember all the steps and prevents you from forgetting to check something.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do when air pressure reaches 125 psi?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It releases air from the tanks.
It starts pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the tanks reach about 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you don't know how to put it out, what should you do?

options.text: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: Do not try to put out a fire if you are unsure how. Move away and let the firefighters handle it. This is especially important if hazardous materials are involved.

questions.question: What does an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) NOT need to include?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number of vehicles passed
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include trip dates and total distance traveled. It does not need to include the number of other vehicles you passed.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts may be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts often means they are loose. Check to make sure they are tight if you see rust.

questions.question: Is looking far ahead while driving a good practice?

options.text: No, there is little you can do about problems far ahead.
Yes, it helps you spot hazards early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards early and respond properly.

questions.question: How can you avoid a hazard?

options.text: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder is the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support large vehicles.

questions.question: What is important to do when making tight turns or maneuvers?

options.text: Open your door to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors, especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.
